primary_claim: The inference cost required to achieve a given score on hard coding benchmarks (WeirdML, Aider Polyglot) has halved roughly every two months over the past two years.

effect.metric: cost to achieve a fixed accuracy threshold on WeirdML / Aider Polyglot (halving time in months)
effect.value: WeirdML: 2.37 (OLS) / 1.99 (Deming) / 1.67 (inverse OLS) months; Aider Polyglot: 2.43 (OLS) / 1.41 (orthogonal) / 1.03 (inverse OLS) months; e.g. GPT-4 (Jun 2023, ~$0.6/task) matched by Llama-3.3-70b at ~$0.0014/task

limitations_stated: Open-model prices from mid-2025 were retroactively attributed to earlier dates, which may bias early open-model cost estimates (though this mainly affects data from 2025 onward).
The order in which models are released can bias the normalized cost curves for a given accuracy threshold.
The different accuracy thresholds share the same underlying models/releases, so they are not independent, and no error bars account for this.
The Aider Polyglot dataset has a shorter historical timeline and lacks results from many small, cheap models that might achieve lower thresholds more cheaply today.
quote: we find that the inference cost to achieve a certain score halves roughly every two monts.
